description: This plot illustrates the relationship between three accuracy metrics—Final Acc, Δ Acc, and Initial Acc—and varying levels of initial confidence. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and features a linear scale ranging from 0.95 to 0.99, with tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.2. The plot includes a background grid of light gray dashed lines corresponding to the major ticks on both axes. The "Final Acc" data is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers that have black outlines and vertical error bars. This line starts at an initial confidence of 0.95 with an accuracy of approximately 0.90, dips slightly to roughly 0.86 at 0.96, gradually rises to a peak of about 0.93 at 0.98, and then declines to approximately 0.88 at 0.99. The "Δ Acc" data is depicted as a dashed orange line with diamond markers, also featuring black outlines and error bars. It begins at 0.95 with a value near 0.90, decreases to about 0.86 at 0.96, increases slightly to approximately 0.88 at 0.97, remains relatively steady near 0.87 at 0.98, and subsequently drops to its lowest point of approximately 0.75 at 0.99. Finally, the "Initial Acc" data is shown as a dash-dot green line with square markers, outlined in black and including error bars. This line starts at 0.95 with an accuracy of roughly 0.00, remains near zero at 0.96, and then exhibits a steady upward trend, reaching approximately 0.01 at 0.97, 0.05 at 0.98, and ending at its highest point of about 0.12 at an initial confidence of 0.99.
